thread:
Priya (Docs): hey folks, opened a small docs PR to align export examples across Ruby SDK + CLI and to tighten SOC2 phrasing around audit exports. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4267 :wave:
Ibrahim (Security): nice. two quick asks: 1) use 'pseudonymize' consistently (avoid 'de-identify' or 'anonymize') and 2) show an explicit TTL format (e.g. 30d) in every example block so customers know units.
Carmen (Legal): +1. for legal we need a short clarifying sentence: "Pseudonymization reduces identifiability but does not always mean irreversible deletion; see footnote." Also avoid words like 'destroyed' or 'permanently' unless we have a retention audit reference.
Priya (Docs): good catches. i'm going to replace the phrase 'anonymize' with 'pseudonymize' and add a footnote. dropping the sample JSON and SDK snippet here for quick review.

JSON example:
{
  "event_type": "user.login",
  "timestamp": "2025-07-10T14:22:31Z",
  "tenant_id": "tenant-7f9",
  "subject": "user_42",
  "fields_pseudonymized": ["email", "ip_address"],
  "retention": "30d",
  "pseudonymize": true
}

Priya (Docs): and an edge-case example where tenant is unknown: 
{
  "event_type": "user.login",
  "tenant_id": null,
  "fields_redacted": ["email"],
  "retention": "90d",
  "pseudonymize": false
}

Tess (SDK): Ruby snippet looks good but our SDK param is `pseudonymize:` not `pseudonymize`. tiny nit: show symbol for keyword arg explicitly.
Ruby SDK sample:
client = Redwood::Client.new(api_key: ENV['REDWOOD_API_KEY'])
client.exports.create(tenant: 'tenant-7f9', scope: 'audit_logs', retention_days: 30, pseudonymize: true)

Ibrahim (Security): also suggest documenting whether pseudonymization uses reversible mapping keys (i.e., held in KMS) or not. maybe a short parenthetical: '(mapping stored: yes|no)'.
Carmen (Legal): for EU customers we should say 'pseudonymization (GDPR-art.4)'. and add: 'If a reversible mapping is stored, customers should treat the export as pseudonymized rather than fully anonymized.'
Priya (Docs): adding both lines. also noticed a broken anchor in the PR: docs/reference/exports.md#cli-usage -> 404. LinkCheckerBot, can you confirm the suggested target?
LinkCheckerBot: found 1 broken link in PR -> docs/reference/exports.md#cli-usage. Suggested fixes: update to /docs/reference/exports/cli.md or add redirect.
CLI-Bot: deployed CLI change in staging to add `--pseudonymize` alias. help text now shows `--pseudonymize   pseudonymize sensitive fields in export (boolean)`
Tess (SDK): patched Ruby example to use keyword arg with symbol, sending tiny PR for snippet update.
Priya (Docs): final copy for the human-facing paragraph: "We pseudonymize fields in audit exports on request; when pseudonymization is not possible, we redact fields and document the limitation. Pseudonymization does not necessarily mean data is irreversibly destroyed." adding footnote link to retention page.
Carmen (Legal): approved with that footnote. please also avoid 'we delete permanently' elsewhere in the docs.
Ibrahim (Security): once PR is updated i'll do a 5-min pass focusing on wording around reversible mappings and retention TTLs.
Priya (Docs): thanks all, i will update the PR: 1) standardize to 'pseudonymize' 2) add TTL examples 30d/90d 3) include tenant-null edge-case 4) fix the CLI link 5) add legal footnote and mapping clarifier. will ping when updated. :sparkles:
